deviations.why_the_rule_was_wrong: distinct-4 falls mechanically with corpus size: common 4-grams repeat more often as texts are added, even when each text is equally diverse. The 0.75 threshold was set from a 50-attack baseline (0.831) and applied to 512 attacks. The same new attacks subsampled to each size give the curve below.
deviations.revised_rule: what the gate was for -- BoN drawing the same attack n times: zero within-cell near-duplicates (word Jaccard > 0.8) AND distinct-4 on 50-attack subsamples within 0.03 of the n=50 baseline
deviations.safeguard: changed before any outcome data existed: no rollout had run and no judge had scored any BoN attack, so the change cannot have been chosen to produce a result. It is a data-quality gate, not a hypothesis rule; every hypothesis and endpoint in results/bon_preregistration.json is untouched, and that file stays frozen.

deviations.issue: At 8 threads the two priciest OpenAI judges (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1) hit organisation TPM limits; ~40-55% of their calls returned level=None after the built-in single retry on the first pass.
deviations.resolution: judge_severity never caches a failure, so re-running at lower concurrency (3, then 2) refilled only the None verdicts. Final state: all 7 judges 0 failures on the main proxy scoring, which is what every hypothesis rests on.
deviations.residual: Self-noise (cache-bypassing, redone in full each pass) never fully cleared for those two judges: 28/64 and 23/64 triples still carried a rate-limit None. Self-agreement is therefore reported over CLEAN triples only, with the None count shown separately: gpt-4o 97% (28 rate-limited), gpt-4.1 100% (23). Among calls that succeeded, both are as self-consistent as the other five judges (91-100%).
deviations.no_frozen_code_touched: src/rubric_judge.py stayed frozen; the fix was the orchestration --workers flag in scripts/bon_judge.py and a clean-triple self-noise metric in scripts/bon_analyze.py, neither of which touches a hypothesis or the estimator.
